FLUX.2 [klein] on Mac: files, RAM and published times

Compact FLUX.2 text-to-image and editing family in 4B and 9B sizes. The 4B model is Apache 2.0; the 9B models use the FLUX Non-Commercial License.

Black Forest Labs · Updated 2026-10-24
Answer

FLUX.2 [klein] runs on a Mac with 96 GB or more. A published run on M2 Ultra · 96 GB used the Klein 4B BF16 build (source, 2026-02-11).

Apache 2.0 (4B), FLUX Non-Commercial License (9B). Commercial use: restricted. Excluded territories: none listed. The 4B model allows commercial use under Apache 2.0. Model use of the 9B models is non-commercial, and filters or manual review are required.

See the exact GGUF files and sizes

Builds here are the distilled 4B and 9B checkpoints. Base 4B, Base 9B and 9B KV are separate checkpoints without their own Mac measurements.

Does it fit your NVIDIA GPU's VRAM?

Runs · Stated means the linked model card, app maker or NVIDIA says a GPU with that much VRAM runs the model; Runs · Published names the card of a dated run. Fits with offload means the main model weights fit in VRAM with a 15% margin but the full set does not: the text encoder and VAE run from system RAM, which is slower. Exceeds VRAM means even the main weights are too large for the card. Mac runs never count here.

Which Mac software routes are listed?

  • ComfyUI

    Official

    Formats: safetensors, gguf. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    On Apple Silicon ComfyUI runs on PyTorch MPS, not MLX. GGUF files need the separate city96/ComfyUI-GGUF custom node. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound: ComfyUI can unload models between stages and publishes no per-model Mac peak.

    Sources: ComfyUI README · ComfyUI system requirements · ComfyUI CLI arguments · ComfyUI-GGUF README

  • Diffusers

    Official

    Formats: safetensors, gguf. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    Runs on the PyTorch mps device on Mac and CUDA on NVIDIA. GGUF loads through from_single_file on the model class, not the pipeline. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound.

    Sources: Diffusers MPS guide · Diffusers GGUF guide

  • Draw Things

    Official

    Formats: safetensors. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    Native offline app for Mac. It picks a weight-streaming tier from physical memory. No official Mac timing or peak-memory table was found, so there is no run verdict here.

    Sources: Draw Things on the App Store · Draw Things App Store listing data · Draw Things model importer

  • flux-2-swift-mlx

    Community

    Formats: safetensors, mlx. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    Swift and MLX app and CLI for FLUX.2. It loads the BF16 transformer from the Black Forest Labs repository and takes the text encoder from separate MLX repositories. Its published peak covers transformer, VAE and activations.

    Sources: flux-2-swift-mlx README · flux-2-swift-mlx model registry

  • mflux

    Community · 0.23.0

    Formats: safetensors. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    MLX-native runner. It reads the original Hugging Face weights and quantizes them while loading (--quantize 3, 4, 5, 6 or 8). --low-ram lowers memory use at a performance cost.

    Install with uv

    uv tool install --upgrade mflux

    Sources: mflux README, install · mflux pyproject · mflux common README, quantization

  • stable-diffusion.cpp

    Official

    Formats: gguf, safetensors. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    C/C++ runner with Metal on Mac and CUDA on NVIDIA. It reads GGUF and safetensors, and its docs keep a page per model family. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound.

    Sources: stable-diffusion.cpp README, backends

What does the official configuration say?

"The 4B card says the model fits in about 13GB VRAM and is accessible on NVIDIA RTX 3090/4070 and above. This is an NVIDIA statement, not a Mac minimum."

Source: FLUX.2 klein 4B model card · Read 2026-10-24.

What known issues should you check?

  • Known issue 1

    Official sources disagree on the 4B VRAM figure: the Hugging Face card says about 13GB, while the reference README says about 8GB without naming a configuration.

    Source: FLUX.2 reference README · Read 2026-10-24

  • Known issue 2

    The 9B card says the model fits in about 29GB VRAM and is accessible on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and above. This is an NVIDIA statement, not a Mac minimum.

    Source: FLUX.2 klein 9B model card · Read 2026-10-24

Frequently asked questions

How fast is FLUX.2 klein on a Mac?

On an M2 Ultra with 96 GB, flux-2-swift-mlx made a 1024x1024 image in 4 steps in 25.6 s for Klein 4B and 54.9 s for Klein 9B at BF16. Peaks were 17.846 GB and 27.779 GB, covering transformer, VAE and activations only.

Is FLUX.2 klein free for commercial use?

The 4B model is Apache 2.0 and allows commercial use. The 9B models use the FLUX Non-Commercial License, which limits model use to non-commercial work, and filters or manual review are required.

How much VRAM does Klein 4B need?

The Hugging Face card says Klein 4B fits in about 13GB VRAM on NVIDIA RTX 3090/4070 and above, while the reference README says about 8GB without naming a configuration. Neither figure is a Mac minimum.
